advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Apply the `_is_gate_exempt_ticket` (or per-event ticket-type) exemption in `_collect_range` so the `--base` merge-gate matches `_collect_all`'s exemption of identity/session_log/code_review.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py:231: `if _is_gate_exempt_ticket(ticket_dir):` — present in `_collect_all` only
`_collect_range` (lines 261-269) iterates diff paths and calls `_event_from_file` with no `_is_gate_exempt_ticket` check
Docstring line 32 of the diff subject / module docstring: 'Skips gate-exempt types (an identity's own CREATE is unsigned by construction).'
_GATE_EXEMPT_TYPES comment lines 96-99: verifying an identity's own CREATE 'would make any store holding an identity fail the merge-gate — self-defeating.'
Held-out tests (tests/unit/test_identity_3183_heldout.py:147,179) only invoke `--all`, so `--base` exemption is untested.
advisory.finding: _collect_range (the `--base` CI merge-gate range path) does not skip gate-exempt ticket types, unlike _collect_all. An identity/session_log/code_review event in the diff range is classified unsigned/unknown-author and fails the gate under require_authenticated, contradicting the module docstring ('Skips gate-exempt types') and the _GATE_EXEMPT_TYPES rationale ('would make any store holding an identity fail the merge-gate — self-defeating').
scenarios: CI runs `rebar verify-authorship --base <ref>` on a PR that creates a new identity ticket, session_log, or code_review with require_authenticated on — the gate fails on the identity's own unsigned CREATE.
advisory.suggested_fix: In `_collect_range`, after resolving `ticket_id`, skip event files whose ticket dir `_is_gate_exempt_ticket(os.path.join(tracker, ticket_id))` — mirroring `_collect_all`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide and document how a ledger entry with a null epoch should be handled (e.g. re-resolve, or distinguish 'epoch-unresolved' from 'bad-signature') rather than silently failing the gate.
evidence: verify_authorship.py:129-134: `if ev.epoch is not None: ... elif ev.position is not None: ... else: return BAD_SIGNATURE`
_ledger_events sets `position=None` and `epoch=entry.get('epoch') if isinstance(entry.get('epoch'), int) else None` (lines 177-179)
compact._build_authorship_ledger records `epoch=None` on any lookup failure (compact.py:98-99) and when `author_id` is falsy (epoch stays None)
advisory.finding: A ledger entry with a null epoch (recorded when `epoch_for_position` failed or returned no author at compaction) is permanently classified BAD_SIGNATURE: in `_verify_signed`, ledger entries have `position=None`, so when `ev.epoch is None` the function falls to the `else: return BAD_SIGNATURE` branch.
scenarios: A signed event whose epoch could not be resolved at compaction (e.g. the repo_root bug above, or a transient lookup failure) is compacted; verify-authorship then reports it bad-signature and fails the gate.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where an identity author carries a decodable-but-invalid author_sig (wrong content and/or wrong key) and assert verify-authorship classifies it `bad-signature` and fails the gate.
evidence: verify_authorship.py:119-120 `if not _is_identity_author(ev.author_id, tracker): return UNKNOWN_AUTHOR`
test_identity_3183_heldout.py:171 `"author_id": "not-a-real-identity",  # present but not an identity ticket` — unknown-author test short-circuits before signature verification
verify_authorship.py:127 `if ev.payload is not None and envelope.payload != ev.payload: return BAD_SIGNATURE` (anti-replay content binding — untested)
verify_authorship.py:138 `return VERIFIED if verdict.verified else BAD_SIGNATURE` (crypto verdict-false branch — untested)
ABSENCE: `search_files 'bad-signature' tests` returns only docstring/comment matches, no assertion on the classification
advisory.finding: The BAD_SIGNATURE classification (the merge-gate's actual security check) is never verified end-to-end. The only 'bad sig' tests either assert replay-never-rejects (test_reducer_never_rejects_bad_signature) or hit the unknown-author short-circuit (test_verify_authorship_flags_unknown_author, whose author_id is not an identity so _is_identity_author returns False at verify_authorship.py:119 before any verification). No test constructs an identity author with a decodable-but-invalid envelope, so neither the content-binding anti-replay check (envelope.payload != ev.payload) nor the epoch-scoped verify_authorship_at_epoch verdict is ever observed to yield BAD_SIGNATURE.
scenarios: A regression that inverts or deletes the content-binding check would let a valid envelope over other content be replayed onto a different event undetected
A regression where verify_authorship_at_epoch always returns verified=True would pass the gate for wrong-key signatures

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test exercising `rebar verify-authorship --base <ref>` that asserts an unsigned event added in the range is flagged (and one outside the range is not).
evidence: verify_authorship.py `_collect_range(tracker, base)` with `run_git(... f"{base}..HEAD")` and `_EMPTY_TREE` fallback
ABSENCE: `search_files '--base' tests` returns no verify-authorship test; all invocations in test_identity_3183*.py use `"--all"`
advisory.finding: The `--base <ref>` / `_collect_range` scope path of verify-authorship — the actual CI commit-range mode — is untested; every test invokes only `--all`. The git-diff collection and the empty-tree fallback (on an unresolvable base / shallow clone) are distinct, security-relevant code paths with no coverage.
scenarios: CI runs verify-authorship with --base <merge-base>; a bug scoping the changed-file range (e.g. missing an added event file, or the empty-tree fallback misbehaving) would let an unsigned event slip the gate

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Enforce content binding for ledger (compacted) events in verify-authorship — persist the signed canonical payload/hash in the authorship ledger and reject when `envelope.payload` does not match it (or verify signatures against event content at compaction and refuse to fold a mismatched signature).
evidence: verify_authorship.py:125-128: `# Content binding (live events only): ...` then `if ev.payload is not None and envelope.payload != ev.payload: return BAD_SIGNATURE`
verify_authorship.py:173-180: ledger `_ScopedEvent(... position=None, payload=None, epoch=...)` — payload is None for every ledger entry, so the binding check at line 127 is skipped
attest/dsse.py:34-57 + attest/authorship.py:52-53: the signature is taken over `pae(PAYLOAD_TYPE, payload)`, i.e. it binds only `envelope.payload`, not the folded event's actual content

compact.py:89-107 `_build_authorship_ledger` copies `author_sig` verbatim ({event_uuid, author_id, author_sig, epoch}) and never verifies it binds this event — no `verify_authorship_at_epoch` / content check at compaction
_ScopedEvent docstring (verify_authorship.py) calls ledger payload 'trusted-at-compaction', but compaction performs no verification, so nothing is actually validated at compaction time

tests/unit/test_identity_3183_heldout.py:123-154 `test_snapshot_roundtrip_signed_events_still_verify` only asserts a correctly-signed event still verifies post-compaction; there is no test that a content-mismatched signature (rejected live) stays rejected after folding
advisory.finding: The verify-authorship merge-gate skips content-binding verification for compacted (ledger) events: `_ledger_events` builds each `_ScopedEvent` with `payload=None`, and `_verify_signed` only checks `envelope.payload != ev.payload` when `ev.payload is not None`. A DSSE signature only binds its own `envelope.payload`, so a signature an author made over different bytes can be attached as `author_sig` of an unrelated folded event and still classify as VERIFIED. The same signature/content mismatch is correctly rejected (BAD_SIGNATURE) while the event is live, so compaction downgrades integrity.
scenarios: An author with a valid key signs event A, then authors a tampered event B and reuses/relabels the valid envelope as B's author_sig; while live B classifies bad-signature, but after `rebar compact` B's ledger entry classifies VERIFIED and the merge-gate passes.
Any store where signed events have been compacted: the merge-gate's tamper-evidence for those events is void because content binding is never re-established from the retired raw bytes.
advisory.suggested_fix: Store the event's canonical payload (or its hash) in each `_build_authorship_ledger` record, populate `_ScopedEvent.payload` for ledger entries from it, and drop the `ev.payload is not None` guard so the `envelope.payload != ev.payload` check runs for both live and ledger events. Alternatively, verify signature-to-content binding at compaction time and omit (or mark bad) any event whose author_sig does not bind its content.
